name: Marie-Pierre Vedrenne
bio: Marie-Pierre Vedrenne, born 13 December 1982 in Limoges, is a French jurist and politician affiliated with the Mouvement Démocrate (MoDem). A specialist in European Union and WTO trade law, she headed the Maison de l'Europe de Rennes before being elected to the European Parliament in 2019 on the Renaissance (La République En Marche / MoDem majority) list. She was re-elected in 2024 in third position on the Besoin d'Europe (Renaissance) list led by Valérie Hayer. In the European Parliament she sat with the Renew Europe group, served as Vice-Chair of the Committee on International Trade (INTA), and was a member of the Bureau of the Renew Europe group; she led the Renaissance delegation within Renew Europe from 2024. She was the European Parliament's lead negotiator (co-rapporteur) on the EU Anti-Coercion Instrument. On 12 October 2025 she joined the second Lecornu government as Minister Delegate to the Minister of the Interior, and after the 26 February 2026 reshuffle she became Minister Delegate to the Minister of the Interior in charge of Citizenship (Citoyenneté). Note: she has not been a Vice-President of the European Parliament; her vice-presidency role was at committee level (INTA).
